title: Stratifying ferroptosis sensitivity in cells and mouse tissues by photochemical activation of lipid peroxidation and fluorescent imaging
protocol: Dissect tissue samples from euthanized mice.
Rinse dissected tissue samples briefly with deionized water.
Snap-freeze the tissue in liquid nitrogen using a foil boat floating on liquid nitrogen.
Use forceps to gently press the foil boat after 5 seconds.
Allow a small volume of liquid nitrogen to flow into the boat until the tissue is completely submerged.
Remove the tissue once the liquid nitrogen has evaporated, covering it with aluminum foil.
Store frozen tissue at −80°C for long-term storage before use.
Transfer frozen tissue to −20°C at least 30 minutes prior to sectioning to equilibrate temperature.
Affix the tissue to the specimen disc using ultrapure water in the cryostat chamber.
Set the optimal cutting temperature for the cryostat.
Adjust the temperature slightly lower for tissues with higher fat deposition.
Maintain the cutting temperature at −20 ± 3°C, e.g., −18°C for kidney and −20°C for brain tissues.
Section the tissue to a thickness of 10 μm (5–15 μm).
Thaw mount sections onto glass slides.
Store mounted tissue section slides at −80°C for long-term storage.
Ensure tissues are kept frozen during cryostat process to minimize metabolic changes.
Keep sections hydrated during cryostat process to facilitate BODIPY-C11 staining.
Equilibrate the tissue section slide to room temperature (22 ± 2°C).
Add 100 μL of BODIPY 581/591 C11 working solution (1×) onto each slide.
Carefully cover samples with coverslips.
Optional: Apply nail polish onto the edge of the coverslip to fix it in place.
For live-cell imaging, replace the culture medium supernatant with an appropriate amount of BODIPY 581/591 C11 working solution prepared with culture medium.
Incubate tissue section or cells with BODIPY-C11 for 30 min.
Keep the section at room temperature during pre-staining process.
Incubate live cells undergoing staining in a cell culture incubator set at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Protect all samples from strong light exposure after BODIPY-C11 addition.
Select a small region of interest of around 2–4 μm² for fluorescence capture.
Utilize the 405 nm high pulse laser from the confocal microscope light source to stimulate the selected region for 5 repeats of 200-ms interval.
Acquire images from the 488 nm (FITC) and 561 nm (TRITC) channels immediately after stimulation.
Place the glass chamber containing BODIPY-C11 pre-stained cells on the microscope stage.
Adjust the focal plane of the microscope.
Set the intensity of 488 nm and 561 nm laser scanning sources.
Adjust the detector voltage to avoid overexposure.
Acquire pre-laser stimulation fluorescent signals from the 488 nm (FITC) channel.
Acquire pre-laser stimulation fluorescent signals from the 561 nm (TRITC) channel.
Select a defined region of interest around 2–4 μm².
Use multiple 800 nm low-energy photons to excite the same target molecule on the focal plane.
Induce lipid peroxidation using the selected laser settings.
Acquire fluorescent signals from the 488 nm (FITC) and 561 nm (TRITC) channels immediately after stimulation.
Set acquisition parameters for the z-axis at intervals of 0.4–0.6 μm but adjust as necessary.
Quantify PALP signals on designated regions of interest.
Analyze the fluorescent signal from the stimulated region using image processing software.
Import the region of interest (ROI) to locate laser bleaching areas.
Measure the gray intensity of pre-PALP 488 nm (Oxpre), pre-PALP 561 nm (Repre), and post-PALP 488 nm (Oxpost) channels.
Exclude post-PALP 561 nm (Repost) channel signal due to potential oxidation and weakening of BODIPY-C11 dye.
Normalize lipid peroxidation signals using the formula: Oxpost / Repre, representing oxidized BODIPY-C11 intensity after stimulation divided by reduced BODIPY-C11 fluorescence before stimulation.
